2 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] (घ) ‘कोयला जनयंत्रक’ से उस रूप में केंरीय सरकार द्वारा कोयला जनयंत्रक संगठन (समूह ‘क’ पद) भती जनयम, 1986 के उपबंधों के अधीन जनयुि व्यजि अजभप्रेत है; (ङ) ‘कोयला खान’ से कोई खान या खुला कायािेत्र अजभप्रेत है, जजसमें कोयले की जिननग या जनष्कषाण, खनन, उत्खनन या उनमें की जा रही संदक्रयाओं का मुख्य उद्देश्य है और जजसके अंतगात कोक के उत्पादन या कोयले के धािन के जलए संयंत्र सजममजलत है; (च) ‘जनपटान’ के अंतगात जनपटान के जलए सहमजत या प्रस्ट्ताि और सांपाजतक जहत, स्ट्िाजमत्ि का अजधकार और कब्जा, चाहे उसके साथ स्ट्िाजमत्ि या दकसी अन्द्य सांपाजतक जहत का जनपटान है या नहीं, सजममजलत है; (छ) ‘कोयला खानों में सुरिा’ कोयला खान के ऊपर सतह पर जस्ट्थत दकसी रेल की सुरिा सजममजलत है; (ज) ‘आकार’ जब उसका उपयोग कोयले के संबंध में दकया जाता है तो उसकी िही जिजनर्ददजियां होंगी, जो भारतीय मानक ब्यूरो द्वारा समय-समय उनकी जिजिजि संख्या आईएस : 437-1979 द्वारा पर दी जाती है; (झ) ‘नौभरण’ बालू या दकसी अन्द्य पदाथा या दोनों से कोयले के उत्खनन द्वारा दकसी कोयला खान में छोडे गए भूजमगत स्ट्थानों को भरने की संदक्रया अजभप्रेत है; (ञ) ‘धािन’ से कोई ऐसी प्रदक्रया या प्रदक्रयाओं का समुच्चय अजभप्रेत है, जो केंरीय सरकार द्वारा इस जनजमत्त अनुमोददत की जाए और जजससे कोयले में पाई गई दकसी संपूणा िेल और खजनज पदाथा अथिा उसके दकसी भाग को उसमें से हटाया जाए; (2) िह िब्द, पद, जो इन जनयमों में प्रयुि हैं, ककतु यहां पररभाजषत नहीं है, का िही अथा होगा, जो उनका अजधजनयम या तदधीन बनाए गए जनयमों में है।”। 3. मूल जनयमों के जनयम 5 के स्ट्थान पर जनम्नजलजखत रखा जाएगा, अथाात् :-- “5. कोयला जनयंत्रक को जििरजणयों और सूचना का प्रस्ट्तुत दकया जाना— (1) प्रत्येक कोयला खान का स्ट्िामी, अजभकताा या प्रबंधक और कोयले के उत्पादन, आपूर्तत और जितरण या व्यापार और िाजणज्य के कारबार में लगा हुआ प्रत्येक व्यजि कोयला जनयंत्रक द्वारा ऐसा जनदेि ददए जाने पर ऐसी जििरजणयां और अन्द्य सूचना, जजसके अंतगात कोयले के उत्पादन के पारेषण, उसकी खानों से उत्पादों की धािन, धािन और प्रदक्रया उत्पाद, उसकी खान या खानों में काया पद्धजत और जस्ट्थजतयों की ऐसे समय के भीतर, जो जनदेि में जिजनर्ददि दकया जाए, प्रस्ट्तुत करेगा । (2) प्रत्येक स्ट्िामी, अजभकताा या प्रबंधक, कोयला जनयंत्रक को दकसी खान, सीम या सीम के अनुभाग को खोलने, पुन: खोलने, बंद करने के संबंध में ऐसी अन्द्य सूचना और कोई अन्द्य सूचना, जो कोयला जनयंत्रक द्वारा अंतरण के जलए जिजहत माध्यम के संबंध में अपेिा की जाए, प्रस्ट्तुत करेगा ।”। 4. मूल जनयमों के जनयम 10 के पश्चात् जनम्नजलजखत जनयम अंत:स्ट्थाजपत दकया जाएगा, अथाात् :-- “10क. खान बंद करने और खान बंद करने के कायाकलाप का जित्तपोषण करने के जलए जिरजचत एस्ट्क्रो खाते की मानीटरी और प्रचालन की िजि—कोयला जनयंत्रक या उसके द्वारा जलजखत में प्राजधकृत कोई अन्द्य अजधकारी इस जनयम की अनुपालना को सुरजित करने की दृजि से,-- (क) कोयला खान के दकसी स्ट्िामी या अजभकताा या प्रबंधक से यह अपेिा कर सकेगा दक िह अनुमोददत खान बंद करने की योजना के कायाान्द्ियन के संबंध में उसके कब्जे में की कोई जानकारी प्रदान करे; (ख) खान में दकए जा रहे बंद करने संबंधी दक्रयाकलापों का जनरीिण करे और खान बंद करने संबंधी योजना की ितों को पूरा करने के जलए दकए जाने िाले दकसी अजतररि काया के जलए जनदेि दे; (ग) कोयला जनयंत्रक खान बंद करने संबंधी अनुपालन प्रमाणपत्र जारी करेगा, जजसके आधार पर पुनरुद्धत पट्टाधृत िेत्र या उस पर कोई संरचना, जजसका उपयोग खान स्ट्िामी के द्वारा नहीं दकया जाना है, अजधकजथत ऐसी प्रदक्रया का पालन करके राज्य सरकार को लौटा दी जाएगी, जो उस समय प्रचलन में है।” 5. मूल जनयम के जनयम 12 के पश्चात् जनम्नजलजखत जनयम अंत:स्ट्थाजपत दकया जाएगा, अथाात् :--

[भागII—खण् ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 3 “12क. कोयला के संरिण और कोयला खानों के जिकास के संबंध में केंरीय सरकार की िजि—(1) केंरीय सरकार, कोयला के संरिण के प्रयोजन के जलए और कोयला खानों के जिकास के जलए ऐसी िजियों का प्रयोग कर सकेगी और ऐसे उपाय कर सकेगी या करिा सकेगी, जो िह आिश्यक या उजचत समझे । (2) पूिागामी िजि की व्यापकता पर प्रजतकूल प्रभाि डाले जबना केंरीय सरकार कोयला खान के स्ट्िामी, अजभकताा या प्रबंधक को जलजखत में संबोजधत आदेि द्वारा उससे अपेिा कर सकेगी दक िह ऐसे उपाय करे, जो िह कोयला के संरिण के प्रयोजन के जलए या कोयला खानों के जिकास के जलए आिश्यक समझे, जजसके अंतगात जनम्नजलजखत हैं,-- (क) दकसी कोयला खान में सुरिा भरणाथा; या (ख) दकसी ऐसे काया का जनिारण, जो कोयला के संरिण या कोयला खान के जिकास पर प्रजतकूल प्रभाि डालता हो; या (ग) कोयला के भस्ट्म तत्िों का लाभ पहुंचाने या उनमें कमी करने की दृजि से कोयला का धािन । (3) केंरीय सरकार, यदद उसका ऐसे सभी तथ्यों और पररजस्ट्थजतयों पर जिचार करने के पश्चात् यह समाधान हो जाता है दक कोयला खान के संबंध में उपजनयम (1) या उपजनयम (2) के अधीन उसके द्वारा दकए गए उपायों, यदद कोई हो, के खचा की िसूली न्द्यायोजचत है तो िह कोयला खान के स्ट्िामी, अजभकताा या प्रबंधक से या तो पूणात: या भागत: ऐसे खचा की िसूली भू-राजस्ट्ि के बकाया के रूप में उसी रीजत में कर सकेगी । 12ख. कोयला खान के संरिण और जिकास के जलए उपाय करने के जलए स्ट्िामी, अजभकताा या प्रबंधक का कताव्य—(1) कोयला खान का स्ट्िामी, अजभकताा या प्रबंधक उसके स्ट्िाजमत्िाधीन प्रत्येक कोयला खान के संबंध में ऐसे उपाय करेगा, जो कोयला के संरिण और कोयला खान के जिकास को सुजनजश्चत करने के जलए आिश्यक हों । (2) उपजनयम (1) के उपबंधों की व्यापकता पर प्रजतकूल प्रभाि डाले जबना कोयला खान का स्ट्िामी अजभकताा या प्रबंधक,-- (क) ऐसे भरण और अन्द्य संदक्रयाएं जनष्पाददत करेगा, जो इस अजधजनयम के उद्देश्यों, जहां तक ऐसे उद्देश्यों का संबंध कोयला के संरिण या कोयला खान के जिकास या कोयला खान से अजभप्राप्त कोयला के उपयोग से है, को अग्रसर करने में आिश्यक हों; (ख) ऐसी भरण और अन्द्य सामग्री अर्तजत करेगा, जो कोयला के संरिण तथा कोयला खान में सुरिा सुजनजश्चत करने के जलए आिश्यक हों; (ग) कोयला के संरिण, कोयला खानों के जिकास और कोयला के उपयोग के संबंध में अनुसंधान करेगा; (घ) िैज्ञाजनक रीजत में कोयला खानों के बारे में योजना बनाएगा और उनका जिकास करेगा । 12ग. कोयला संरिण और जिकास सलाहकार सजमजत—(1) केंरीय सरकार, कोयला खान संरिण और जिकास लेखा के उधार की राजि के संजितरण के जलए प्रदक्रया अिधारण करने के प्रयोजन के जलए, सरकार को सलाह देने के जलए “कोयला संरिण और जिकास सलाहकार सजमजत” नामक एक सलाहकार सजमजत गरठत कर सकेगी । (2) सलाहकार सजमजत जनम्नजलजखत सदस्ट्यों से जमलकर बनेगी, अथाात् :-- (i) अपर सजचि (कोयला), कोयला मंत्रालय, पदेन, जो अध्यि होगा; (ii) जित्तीय सलाहकार और संयुि सजचि, कोयला मंत्रालय, पदेन – सदस्ट्य; (iii) सलाहकार (पररयोजनाएं), कोयला मंत्रालय - सदस्ट्य; (iv) खान सुरिा महाजनदेिक, श्रम मंत्रालय, पदेन - सदस्ट्य; (v) िररष्ठ सलाहकार (ऊजाा), नीजत आयोग - सदस्ट्य; (vi) अध्यि-सह-प्रबन्द्ध जनदेिक, बीसीसीएल - सदस्ट्य; (vii) अध्यि-सह-प्रबन्द्ध जनदेिक, ईसीएल - सदस्ट्य; (viii) अध्यि-सह-प्रबन्द्ध जनदेिक, केन्द्रीय खान योजना और जडजाइन संस्ट्थान - सदस्ट्य;

4 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] (ix) जनदेिक (तकनीकी), कोल इंजडया जलजमटेड - सदस्ट्य; (x) जनदेिक (तकनीकी), एससीसीएल - सदस्ट्य; (xi) जनदेिक, केन्द्रीय खनन और ईंधन अनुसंधान संस्ट्थान, धनबाद, पदेन - सदस्ट्य; (xii) कोयला जनयंत्रक, कोयला मंत्रालय – सदस्ट्य सजचि; (xiii) केन्द्रीय सरकार द्वारा नामजनर्ददि दकए जाने िाले प्राइिेट या कैजटटि कोयला उत्पादन संगठनों के दो प्रजतजनजध । (3) उपजनयम (1) में अन्द्तर्तिि उपबंधों की व्यापकता पर प्रजतकूल प्रभाि डाले जबना, कोयला संरिण और जिकास सलाहकारी सजमजत – (क) केन्द्रीय खान योजना और जडजाइन संस्ट्थान या इस जनजमत्त जिजनर्ददि दकसी अन्द्य प्राजधकारी द्वारा इस संबंध में की जा सकने िाली जसफाररि को दृजिगत रखते हुए, देि के कोयला भंडारों के संरिण, जिकास और िैज्ञाजनक उपयोग के संबंध में राष्ट्रीय नीजत जिरजचत करने तथा उसके कायाान्द्ियन के संबंध में केन्द्रीय सरकार को सलाह देगी ; (ख) उन उपायों की जसफाररि करेगी जजन्द्हें – (i) कोयला संसाधनों का संरिण सुजनजश्चत करने के जलए दकया जाना चाजहए, (ii) िैज्ञाजनक रीजत में कोयला खानों का जिकास करने के जलए दकया जाना चाजहए, (iii) कोयले के संरिण, कोयला खानों के जिकास तथा कोयले के उपयोग के संबंध में अनुसंधान करने के जलए दकया जाना चाजहए, (iv) कोयले की खान बन्द्द करने की योजना (जलग्नाईट समेत) पर राष्ट्रीय नीजत जिरजचत करने तथा उसके कायाान्द्ियन के जलए दकया जाना चाजहए, (v) कोयले के बेहतर उपयोग के जलए दकया जाना चाजहए ; (ग) उन िगों, श्रेणी या आकारों की जसफाररि करेगी जजनमें कोयला या कोक प्रिगीकृत दकया जा सकेगा; (घ) जिजनर्ददि प्रयोजनों के जलए कोयला खानों के स्ट्िाजमयों, अजभकतााओं या प्रबन्द्धकों को अथिा दकसी अन्द्य व्यजि को जित्तीय सहायता स्ट्कीम के अधीन जनजधयों के जितरण पर केन्द्रीय सरकार को सलाह देगी; (ङ) केन्द्रीय सरकार को उस रीजत जजसमें तथा िह िता जजसके अधीन जित्तीय सहायता अनुदत्त की जाएगी, पर सलाह देगी; (च) यह सुजनजश्चत करने के जलए दक क्या जित्तीय सहायता का उपयोग उस प्रयोजन के जलए जजसके जलए इसे स्ट्िीकृत दकया गया था, दकया जा रहा है या दकया गया है, तथा यह सुजनजश्चत करने के जलए भी दक क्या इसके अधीन दकए गए उपबंध का पालन दकया जा रहा है, परीिण, जांचों और जनरीिण करने के जलए केन्द्रीय सरकार को उस प्रदक्रया के संबंध में सलाह देगी जो अंगीकृत की जानी चाजहए; (छ) केन्द्रीय सरकार को उस कारािाई की जसफाररि करेगी जो उस व्यजियों के जिरुद्ध की जानी चाजहए जो उपबंधों के अनुपालन में तथा स्ट्कीमों के कायाान्द्ियन में भी कोई व्यजतक्रम करते हैं तथा कोयला खानों के संरिण और जिकास के जलए उपाय हेतु जसफाररि करेगी । (4) कोयला संरिण और जिकास सलाहकारी सजमजत, जब कभी भी केन्द्रीय सरकार द्वारा ऐसा करना अपेजित हो, बैठक करेगी तथा उसे स्ट्ियं की प्रदक्रया जिजनयजमत करने की िजि होगी । (5)  कोयला संरिण और जिकास सलाहकारी सजमजत का गठन न होना या उसमें कोई ररजि से कोयला खान संरिण और जिकास खाते में जमा होने िाली राजियों में से दकन्द्हीं रकमों का जितरण या उपयोजन अजिजधमान्द्य नहीं होगा । 12घ. िे प्रयोजन जजनके जलए जनजधयों का जितरण दकया जा सकेगा – केन्द्रीय सरकार, कोयला संरिण और जिकास सलाहकारी सजमजत की जसफाररिों का ध्यान रखते हुए, जनम्नजलजखत एक या अजधक प्रयोजनों के जलए कोयला खानों के स्ट्िाजमयों, अजभकतााओं या प्रबन्द्धक अथिा दकसी अन्द्य व्यजि को जितरण कर सकेगी, अथाात्:-- (1) संरिण और सुरिा --

[भागII—खण् ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 5 (क) भरण प्रचालन । (ख) संरिण काया जजसमें जनम्नजलजखत सजममजलत हैं – (i) अज्िलनिील सामजग्रयों से लपेटना; (ii) धसान को भरना; (iii) िाखा खंदकों को काटना; (ग) सतह संरिण उपाय जजसके अन्द्तगात धसान के िेत्रों के ऊपर भिनों और संरचनाओं को खाली करना तथा प्रभाजित व्यजियों का पुनिाास; (घ) भरण टलांटों, ब्लैंजडग टलांटों तथा कोयले के पररष्करण के जलए टलांटों को लगाना; (ङ) बालू को प्राप्त करने तथा उसके पररिहन के जलए स्ट्कीमें । (2) कोयला खानों का िैज्ञाजनक जिकास – (क) नई कोयला खनन पद्धजतयों का जिकास, जिस्ट्फोटकों का जिकास और उपयोग; (ख) खानों में जिजभन्न भूजमगत और सतही पररिहन प्रणाजलयों के तकनीकी-आर्तथक अध्ययन; (ग) गहरी खानों में चट्टानों के फटने की समस्ट्याओं का अन्द्िेषण; (घ) जिजभन्न खनन दिाओं के अधीन रूफ बोनल्कग का अन्द्िेषण; (ङ) मेन राईनडग जसस्ट्टम का आरमभ; (च) खनन में उपयोजन हेतु आईटी तथा अन्द्य इलैक्राजनक सहायताएं । (3) अनुसंधान और जिकास – (क) भरण सामग्री का पररिहन; (ख) खानों में भरण के जलए अपजिि सामजग्रयों की उपयुिता का अन्द्िेषण; (ग) खान में अजग्न दुघाटना की समस्ट्या का अन्द्िेषण तथा उन्द्हें जनयंजत्रत करने िाली जिजभन्न पद्धजतयों की प्रभाव्यता; (घ) खानों में िातायन तथा अन्द्य पयाािरणीय दिाओं का मूल्यांकन; (ङ) जमथेन उत्सजान तथा अत्यंत गैसीय कोयला दरारों से अपिहन; (च) खनन िेत्रों में सतह प्रदूषण तथा पयाािरणीय जनयंत्रण पर अनुसंधान; (छ) केन्द्रीय सरकार द्वारा यथाजनदेजित संरिण की िृजद्ध के जलए कोई अन्द्य दक्रयाकलाप; (4) सलाहकारी सजमजत के काया के संबंध में व्ययों को पूरा करना (5) सडक मागों का जिकास तथा रेल अिसंरचना का सृजन । 12.ड सहायता के जलए आिेदन: 12.(घ) में उजल्लजखत प्रयोजनों के जलए जित्तीय सहायता प्राप्त करने के इच्छुक कोयला खान के प्रत्येक स्ट्िामी, अजभकताा या प्रबंधक या दकसी अन्द्य व्यजि को कोयला संरिण और जिकास सलाहकार सजमजत द्वारा यथाजिजनर्ददि प्ररूप में कोयला जनयंत्रक के समि आिेदन प्रस्ट्तुत करना होगा। 12.च सहायता की मात्रा—केन्द्रीय सरकार द्वारा प्रत्येक मामले की पररजस्ट्थजतयों को ध्यान में रखते हुए सहायता प्रदान की जाएगी। 12.छ सहायता अनुदत्त करने की ितों की स्ट्िकृजत—केन्द्रीय सरकार, इन जनयमों के अधीन सहायता अनुदत्त करने से पहले कोयला खान के स्ट्िामी, अजभकताा या प्रबंधक या दकसी अन्द्य व्यजि द्वारा जजन्द्हें सहायता अनुदत्त करने का प्रस्ट्ताि है पूरी की जाने िाली ितें जिजनर्ददि करेगी और ऐसे स्ट्िामी द्वारा ऐसी ितों की स्ट्िीकृजत को जलजखत रूप में सुरजित करेगी।

6 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 12.ज िार्तषक ररपोटा का जनिेदन—प्रत्येक व्यजि जजसे धन संजितररत दकया गया है प्रजत िषा 30 जसतंबर तक कोयला जनयंत्रक को कोयला खान संरिण और जिकास खाता के संबंध मे संपरीिक की ररपोटा और कोयला जनयंत्रक द्वारा जिजनर्ददि प्रारूप में प्राजप्त और संदाय के जििरण के साथ साथ। प्राजप्त और संदाय के जििरण की प्रजत के साथ जपछले जित्तीय िषा के दौरान प्राप्त सहायता के उपयोग से संबंजधत एक िार्तषक ररपोटा प्रस्ट्तुत करेगा।'' [फा. सं. 12012/3/2021-पीएस-1] भबानी प्रसाद पजत, संयुि सजचि

MINISTRY OF COAL NOTIFICATION New Delhi, the 9th August, 2021 G.S.R. 546(E). —In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 18 of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 (67 of 1957), the Central Government hereby makes the following rules to amend the Colliery Control Rules, 2004, namely:— 1. Short title and commencement. — (1) These rules may be called the Colliery Control (Amendment) Rules, 2021. (2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 2. In the Colliery Control Rules, 2004 (hereinafter referred to as the principal rules), for rule 2, the following rule shall be substituted, namely:— ―2. Definitions. — (1) In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires, — (a) ‗Act‘ means the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 (67 of 1957); (b)      ‗agent‘, ‗manager‘ and ‗owner‘ when used in relation to a colliery shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in Mines Act, 1952; (c) ‗coal‘ includes anthracite, bituminous coal, lignite, peat and any other form of carbonaceous matter sold or marketed as opal and also coke; (d)        ‗Coal Controller‘ means the person appointed as such by the Central Government under the provisions of the Coal Controller‘s Organisation (Group ‗A‘ Posts) Recruitment Rules, 1986; (e) ‗colliery‘ means any mine or open working where winning or extraction of coal is the principal object of the mining, quarrying or any other operation carried on therein and includes a plant for production of coke or for the washing of coal; (f) ‗disposal‘ includes agreeing or offering to dispose of, and the disposal of ownership or any proprietary interest, the right of possession and possession whether or not accompanied by any disposal of ownership or any other proprietary interest; (g) ‗safety in coal mines‘ includes the safety of any railway situated on the surface above coal mine; (h) ‗size‘ when used in relation to coal shall have the same specifications as given, from time to time, by the Bureau of Indian Standards in their specifications number IS: 437-1979; (i)        ‗stowing‘ means operation of filling with sand or any other material, or with both, spaces left underground in a coal mine by extraction of coal; (j)        ‗washing‘ means such process or combination of processes as may be approved in this behalf by the Central Government by which the whole or any part of the shale and minerals matter found in the coal is removed therefrom. (2) The words, expressions used in these rules but not defined herein shall have the same meaning as referred to them in the Act or rules made thereunder.‖ 3. In the principal rules, for Rule 5, following shall be substituted, namely:— ―5. Submission of returns and information to Coal Controller.— (1) Every owner, agent or manager of a colliery and every person engaged in the business of production, supply and distribution of, or trade and commerce in coal, on being directed to do so by the Coal

[भागII—खण् ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 7 Controller shall submit such returns and other information including information regarding production of dispatch of coal, washery products from his mines, washery and process products, working methods and conditions in his mine or mines, within such time, as may be specified in the direction. (2) Every owner, agent or manager shall furnish to the Coal Controller such other information regarding opening, re-opening, closure of mine, seam or section of seam and any other information as may be required by the Coal Controller in respect of prescribed media for transfer.‖. 4. In the principal rules, after rule 10, the following rule shall be inserted, namely.— "10A. Power to Monitor Mine Closure and operate the escrow account formed for funding Mine Closure Activity – The Coal Controller or any other officer authorised by him in writing may with a view to securing compliance of this rule, - (a) require any owner or agent or manager of a colliery to give any information in his possession regarding to implementation of approved mine closure plan; (b) inspect the closure activities being conducted at the mine and direct for any additional jobs to be carried out to fulfil the conditions of Mine Closure Plan; (c) Coal Controller shall issue Mine Closure Compliance Certificates based on which the reclaimed leasehold area or any structure thereon which is not to be utilised by the mine owner shall be surrendered to the State Government following a laid down procedure which are in vogue at that point of time." 5. In the principal rules, after rule 12, the following rules shall be inserted, namely:— "12A. Power of Central Government in respect of conservation of coal and development of coal mines.—(1) The Central Government may, for the purpose of conservation of coal and for the development of coal mines, exercise such powers and take, or cause to be taken, such measures as it may deem necessary or proper. (2) Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, the Central Government may, by order in writing addressed to the owner, agent or manager of a coal mine, require him to take such measures as it may think necessary for the purpose of conservation of coal or for development of coal mines, including— (a) in any coal mine, stowing for safety; or (b) the prevention of any factor which may adversely affect the conservation of coal or development of coal mine; or (c) washing of coal with a view to beneficiating and reducing the ash-contents of coal. (3) The Central Government may, if it is satisfied after consideration of all the facts and circumstances that the recovery of the cost of measures, if any, undertaken by it under sub-rule (1) or sub-rule (2) in relation to a coal mine is justified, recover such cost from the owner, agent or manager of the coal mine, either wholly or partly, in the same manner as an arrear of land revenue. 12B. Duty of owner, agent or manager to take steps for the conservation and development of coal mine.—(1) The owner, agent or manager of a coal mine shall take, in relation to each coal mine owned by him, such steps as may be necessary to ensure the conservation of coal and development of the coal mine. (2) Without prejudice to the generality of the provisions of sub-rule(1), the owner, agent or manager of a coal mine shall— (a) execute such stowing and other operations as may be necessary to be taken in furtherance of the objects of the Act in so far as such objects relate to the conservation of coal or development of the coal mine or the utilisation of coal obtained from the coal mine; (b) acquire such stowing and other materials as may be necessary for ensuring the conservation of coal, and safety in, the coal mine; (c) undertake research in relation to conservation of coal, development of coal mines and utilisation of coal; (d) plan and undertake development of the coal mines in a scientific manner. 12C. Coal Conservation and Development Advisory Committee. — (1) For the purpose of determining the procedure for the disbursement of sums of the credit of the Coal Mines Conservation and Development Account, the Central Government may constitute an Advisory Committee, to be called the ―Coal Conservation and Development Advisory Committee‖ to advise  the Government. (2) The Advisory Committee shall consist of the following members, namely: — (i)    Additional Secretary (Coal), Ministry of Coal, ex-officio who shall be the Chairman; (ii)    Financial Adviser and Joint Secretary, Ministry of Coal, ex-officio -member; (iii)    Advisor (Projects), Ministry of Coal- member;

8 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] (iv)    Director General of Mine Safety, Ministry of Labour, ex-officio member; (v)      Sr. Advisor (Energy), NitiAayog- member; (vi)     Chairman-cum-Managing Director, BCCL- member; (vii)    Chairman-cum-Managing Director, ECL-member; (viii)   Chairman-cum-Managing Director, Central Mine Planning and DesignInstitute- member; (ix)    Director (Technical), Coal India Ltd.- member; (x)     Director (Technical), SCCL-member; (xi)     Director, Central Institute of Mining & Fuel Research, Dhanbad, ex-officio member; (xii)   Coal Controller, Ministry of Coal – member secretary; (xiii)    Two representatives of private or captive coal producing organisations to benominated by the Central Government. (3) Without prejudice to the generality of the provisions contained in sub-rule (1), the Coal Conservation and Development Advisory Committee shall— (a)  advise the Central Government regarding the formulation and implementation of a national policy in relation to the conservation, development and scientific utilization of the coal reserves of the country keeping in view the recommendation that may be made in this regard by the Central Mine Planning and Design Institute or any other authority specified on its behalf; (b)   recommend measures which should be taken for— (i)    ensuring the conservation of the coal resources, (ii)   undertaking the development of the coal mines in a scientific manner, (iii)   undertaking research in relation to conservation of coal, development of coal mines and utilisation of coal, (iv)  undertaking formulation and implementation of national policy on Mine Closure Plan of Coal (including Lignite) mines; and (v)   better utilisation of coal; (c) recommend the classes, grade or sizes into which coal or coke may be categorised; (d)          advise the Central Government on the disbursement of funds under financial assistance scheme to the owners, agents or managers of coal mines or to any other person for specified purposes; (e)            advise the Central Government on the manner in which and the condition, subject to which financial assistance shall be granted; (f)            advise the Central Government regarding the procedure that should be adopted for carrying out examination, inquiries and inspection in order to ascertain whether the financial assistance is being or has been utilised for the purpose for which it was sanctioned, as also to ascertain whether the provision made thereunder are being complied with; (g)            recommend to the Central Government the action that should be taken against those who make any default in complying with the provisions, and also in implementing the schemes and measures for conservation and development of coal mines. (4) The Coal Conservation and Development Advisory Committee shall meet as and  when required by the Central Government to do so and shall have the power to regulate its own procedure. (5) The non-constitution of the Coal Conservation and Development Advisory Committee or the existence of any vacancy therein shall not render invalid the disbursement or application of any amounts out of the sums standing to the credit of the Coal Mines Conservation and Development Account. 12D. Purposes for which funds may be disbursed.—  The Central Government may, having regard to the recommendations of the Coal Conservation and Development Advisory Committee, make disbursements to the owners, agents or manager of coal mines or to any other person, for the purposes, one or more of the following, namely : — (1) Conservation and safety- (a) Stowing operations. (b) Protective Works, including- (i) blanketing with incombustible materials;

[भागII—खण् ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 9 (ii) filling up of subsidence; (iii) cutting of branch trenches; (c) Surface protection measures including vacation of buildings and structures over areas of subsidence and rehabilitation of affected persons; (d) Installation of stowing plants, blending plants and plants for the beneficiation of coal; (e) Schemes for recovery and transportation of sand. (2) Scientific Development of Coal Mines — (a)     Development of new coal mining methods, development andutilisation of explosives; (b)    Techno-economic studies of various underground and surface transport systems in mines; (c)    Investigation into problems of rock burst in deep mines; (d)    Investigation into roof bolting under different mining conditions; (e)    Introduction of man riding system; (f)     IT and other electronic aids for application in mining. (3) Research and Development— (a)    Transportation of stowing material; (b)   Investigations into suitability of waste materials for stowing in mines; (c)   Investigation into problems of mines fires and efficacy of different methods of dealing with them; (d)   Assessment of ventilation and other environmental condition in mines; (e)    Problems relating to Methane emission and drainage from highly gassy coal seams; (f)    Research on surface pollution and environmental control in mining areas; (g)    Any other activity for furtherance of conservation as directed by the Central Government; (4) Meeting the expenses in connection with the work of Advisory Committee (5)  Development of roads and creation of rail infrastructure. 12E. Application For Assistance.— Every owner, agent or manager of a coal mine or group of coal mines or any other person, desirous of obtaining financial assistance for purposes mentioned in  rule 12D, shall submit his application to the Coal Controller in the form as may be specified by the Coal Conservation and Development Advisory committee. 12F.  Quantum of Assistance.—TheAssistance shall be granted by the Central Government with due regard to the circumstances of each case. 12G. Acceptance of Conditions Attaching to the Grant Of Assistance.– Before granting assistance under these rules, the Central Government may specify the conditions to be fulfilled by the owner, agent or manager of a coal mine or any other person to whom assistance is proposed to be granted and secure the acceptance in writing by such owner, agent or manager of the coal mine or any other person of such conditions. 12H. Submission of Annual Reports.– Every person to whom the money has been disbursed shall submit to the Coal Controller by 30th September in each year an Annual Report regarding the utilisation of the assistance received by him during the previous financial year along with a copy of the statement of Receipts and Payments, together with the Auditor‘s Report in respect of the Coal Mines Conservation and Development Account and the Statement of Receipts and Payments in the form as may be specified by the Coal Controller.‖ [No.12012/3/2021-PS-I] BHABANI PRASAD PATI, Jt Secy. The Principal rules were published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary under Part II, Section 3, Sub Section (i) vide number GSR 540  (E), dated the 25th August 2004.

MINISTRY OF COAL NOTIFICATION New Delhi, the 29th May, 2020 S.O. 1694(E).—In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 26 of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 (67 of 1957) and in supersession of the notifications of the Government of India, Ministry of Coal published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub- section (ii) vide number S.O.2265 (E), dated the 4th  June, 2018, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the Central Government hereby directs that,— 1.(a) on and from the date of publication of this notification and upto the expiry of a period of nine months from the commencement of the Mineral Concession (Amendment) Rules, 2020, the power to approve mining plan for all categories of coal and lignite and sand mining for stowing, exercisable by the Central Government under clause (b) of sub-section (2) of section 5 of the Act, shall also be exercisable by the Project Adviser, Ministry of Coal; (b) on and from the expiry of aperiod of nine months from the commencement of the Mineral Concession (Amendment) Rules, 2020, the power to approve mining planfor all categories of coal and lignite and sand mining for stowing, exercisable by the Central Government under clause (b) of sub-section (2) of section 5 of the Act, shall also be exercisable by the Coal Controller, Kolkata, (Coal Controller’s Organization being a subordinate office of the Government of India in the Ministry of Coal). 2. On and from the date of publication of this notification, any person aggrieved by any orders made or directions issued in respect of mining plan by an officer designated above may, apply to Secretary to Government of India, Ministry of Coal, for revision of such order made or directions issued thereon. [F. No. 34011/28/2019-CPAM] BHABANI PRASAD PATI, Jt. Secy.

### Content

No.: CPAM-34011/28/2019-CPAM(343762) Government of India Ministry of Coal [MPS Section] GPOA-3, Room No 4605, Netaji Nagar New Delhi,  31st    July 2026 NOTICE

Subject: Stakeholders consultation on Draft Guidelines for preparation of Mining Plan and Mine Closure Plan for Coal and Lignite Mines, 2026.

The Guidelines for preparation of Mining Plan and Mine Closure Plan for Coal and Lignite Blocks, 2025 dated 31.01.2025 may kindly be referred to. In this regard, it is stated that these guidelines are being revised and new guidelines has been drafted as Guidelines for preparation of Mining Plan and Mine Closure Plan for Coal and Lignite Mines, 2026.  These draft guidelines are available on the website of the Ministry of Coal and Coal Controller's Organization. 2.    Requisite suggestions/comments, if any, may be furnished to Ministry of Coal on email id : socrc.moc@nic.in within 15 days, in the following format : S.No.        Clause No. Suggested modification Rationale

Encl: as above (Alok Verma) Under Secretary to the Government of India Email: alok.verma07@gov.in

To 1. Secretary, Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change 2. DG, DGMS 3. CMDs of CIL/SCCL/NLCIL 4. Coal Controller, New Delhi 5. Director (Nominated Authority)- For circulation to all coal companies except CIL/SCCL/NLCIL Copy to: 1. NIC- with request to upload the above document on the website of the Ministry of Coal. 2. Coal Controller Organization - with request to upload the above documents CPAM-34011/28/2019-CPAM I/41283/2026

on the website of CCO. 3. DS (Admin), MoC- with request to issue a small public notice in newspapers informing that the document is available at the website for comments. CPAM-34011/28/2019-CPAM I/41283/2026

Draft Mining Plan Guidelines for Coal and Lignite Mine 2026

List of Abbreviations

APA = Accredited Prospecting Agency CBDPA= Coal Block Development and Production Agreement CPCB = Central Pollution Control Board CCO = Coal Controller Organisation CIL= Coal India Ltd. Crs= Crores =10 million CMDPA = Coal Mine Development and Production Agreement CMPDIL = Central Mine Planning and Design Institute Limited DGPS = Differential Global Positioning System DGMS = Directorate General of Mines Safety ERA = Expert Review Agency EC = Environment Clearance FC = Forest Clearance GR = Geological Report Ha = Hectare IIT = Indian Institute of Technology ISM = Indian School of Mines Km = Kilometre LBDPA= Lignite Block Development and Production Agreement LS = Lumpsum m = Metre Max = Maximum MCDR = Mineral Conservation and Development Rules Mt = Million Tonne MTPA = Millian Tonne Per Annum ML = Mining Lease MoEFCC = Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change MCR = Mineral (Other than Atomic and Hydrocarbons Energy Minerals) Concession Rules, 1960

Mm3 = Million Cubic Meters MoC = Ministry of Coal MPPA = Mining Plan Preparing Agency NABET = National Accreditation Board for Education and Training NLCIL = NLC India Limited NEERI = National Environmental Engineering Research Institute OC = Opencast OB = Overburden OBR= OB Removal PAPs= Project Affected Persons PL = Prospecting Licence PWD = Public Works Department PSP = Pump Storage Projects PRC= Peak Rated Capacity QCI = Quality Council of India QP = Qualified Person SCCL = Singareni Collieries Company Limited SR = Stripping Ratio SPCB = State Pollution Control Board SWCS= Single Window Clearance System t = Tonne UG = Underground WGS84 = World Geodetic System 1984 WPI = Wholesale Price Index w.r.t= with respect to

Fl. No. CPAM-34011/28/2019-CPAM [E-343762] Government of India Ministry of Coal [MPS Section] Shastri Bhawan, New Delhi July, 2026 OFFICE MEMORANDUM

Subject: Guidelines for preparation of Mining Plan and Mine Closure Plan for Coal and Lignite Mines, 2026.

Chapter-I Preliminary

1.1. Short title and commencement. - (a) These guidelines may be called the “Guidelines for preparation of Mining Plan and Mine Closure Plan for Coal and Lignite Mines, 2026”. (b) These Guidelines shall come into force 30 days from date of issue of these guidelines. Provided that the Mining Plans uploaded on SWCS portal (https://swcs.coal.gov.in) before coming into force of these guidelines shall continue to be governed by the guidelines dated 31.01.2025. (c) The Mine Closure Plan, inclusive of the Progressive Mine Closure Plan and Final Mine Closure Plan, shall constitute an integral component of the Mining Plan. (d) “Guidelines for preparation and approval of Mining Plan for Coal and Lignite Blocks/Mines for Underground Gasification 2026” as amended from time to time shall be an integral part of this guideline. 1.2. Objectives: (a) To optimize the extraction of coal and lignite resources that minimize waste generation while maximizing efficiency. (b) To emphasize the importance of systematic and scientific mining, to promote safety and health, to safeguard the interest of workers and local communities, to promote upgradation of infrastructure and adoption of global best technologies. (c) To promote responsible mining practices that support both the coal and lignite industry and the broader ecosystem by incorporating restoration, remediation, and regeneration measures into mining plans for sustainable management of natural resources. (d) To prioritize environmental conservation by monitoring soil, groundwater, and vegetation and implementing measures to improve air, soil and water quality. 1.3. Definitions: In these guidelines, unless the context otherwise requires: (a) “Abandoned Mine” means such mine as has been abandoned with no intention of working in the future; (b) “Discontinued Mine” means such mine as has been discontinued for any reason and are inaccessible or rendered inaccessible but are likely to be worked again.

(c) “Escrow account” means an account opened by the project proponent in a scheduled commercial bank, facilitating the deposition and withdrawal of funds for mine closure purposes; (d) “First-mile connectivity” means seamless movement of coal from the mine to the dispatch point with minimum road transport and mechanized loading onto railway rakes. It shall also include direct coal transfer to the consumer through conveyors, rails or any other mechanized means; (e) “Leased Area” shall have the same meaning as defined in Section 3 (ac) of MMDR, Act, 1957; (f) “Life of the Mine” means the period starting from the date of receiving mine opening permission and till end of post closure monitoring period; (g) “Mine closure” means the comprehensive process of closing and securing a mine during development and production period and upon completion of post closure monitoring period; (h) “Mine Closure Plan” means a document that includes financial provisions and activities to be implemented towards mine closure during development and production period and till final mine closure; (i) “Minor Changes” shall have the same meaning as prescribed in sub-rule (2) of Rule 22-E of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960 as amended from time to time; (j) “Post closure monitoring period” means the period of 2 (two) years after completion of the post mining closure period; (k)  “Post mining closure period” means the period of 3 (three) years after cessation of the production activities; (l) “Production Life of the Mine” means the period of development and production years as given in the calendar plan; and (m) “Project Area” means the total area of the mine (as defined in the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions, Code, 2020) specified in the mining plan and includes the area required for overburden dumping and associated infrastructure such as office premises, residential areas, R&R colonies, outside the mining lease area; 1.4. Requirement and Applicability: (a) These guidelines supersede all previous guidelines including “Guidelines for preparation of Mining Plan and Mine Closure Plan for Coal and Lignite blocks, 2025” dated 31.01.2025. Provided that the “Guidelines for the Management of discontinued/abandoned/closed mines before the year 2009” dated 28.10.2022 shall continue to remain valid. (b) Every coal or lignite mine shall have a Mining Plan approved by the Coal Controller based on which mining operations shall be carried out . Provided that the Mining Plan of coal/lignite mines of Central Public Sector Undertakings, the State Public Sector Undertakings, Damodar Valley Corporation and SCCL, when the same is prepared by CMPDIL, may be approved by the respective Board. Provided further that Mining plans not required to be approved by the Coal Controller, shall be uploaded on SWCS portal within one month of approval by respective Boards. (c) No coal or lignite block shall be operational without an approved Mining Plan. (d) The approved Mining Plan shall be valid for the life of the mine.

Provided that the competent authority may approve any revision(s) or modification(s) of the Mining Plan, and upon such approval, the revised or modified Mining Plan, as the case may be, shall remain valid for remaining part of the life of the mine. (e) These guidelines shall apply to all coal and lignite mines including sand mining for use of stowing in mines and Mining Plans for sand mining for the cited use shall be prepared in accordance with the norms prescribed by the respective states. Provided that in the event that a state has not formulated such norms, a sample format for preparation of Mining Plan and submission of information to the Coal Controller is attached at Appendix-I. The process for approval of such Mining Plan shall be as at Chapter-IV of the guidelines. (f) All abandoned mines and discontinued mines since 27th August 2009 shall achieve mine closure as per provisions of these guidelines. (g) All discontinued mines, abandoned mines and closed mines upto 26th August 2009 shall achieve mine closure as per provisions of “Guidelines for the Management of discontinued/abandoned/closed mines before the year 2009” dated 28.10.2022. (h) All Mining Plans approved under provisions of previous guidelines shall be deemed to have been approved under these guidelines. Provided that any modification or revision in approved Mining Plans shall be in accordance with provisions of these guidelines. (i) A Mining Plan may be formulated for multiple leased areas, or a leased area may have multiple Mining Plans. Chapter-II Mining Plan (excluding mine closure plan) 2.1. The Mining Plan shall be formulated as per approved Geological Report. The geological report shall take into account the prevailing ISP norms and guidelines/ directives issued by the Central Government. 2.2. Components of Mining Plan: 2.2.1. General: (a) The Mining Plan will take into account the project's location, detail of allotment or allocation, previous approval of the Mining Plan (if any), surface features of the block/mine, brief socio- economic information. (b) In case of unexplored/ partially explored blocks, the project proponent shall decide the appropriate Mining Method (Opencast or Underground or Mixed Mining and/or Underground Coal Gasification) and suitable technology to carry out mining operations so as to achieve optimum extraction of coal or lignite while ensuring safe and sustainable resource management. The project proponent may provide an analysis as regards arriving on appropriate mining method. (c) Mining Plan shall contain year-wise calendar plan and indicative production of coal or lignite as well as removal of overburden along with stage plan for critical years such as 1st year, 5th

year, the year of achieving rated capacity of the mine, 10th year, 30th year and the final year (i.e. at the end of mine life). Provided that a block/mine may increase annual coal production upto rated capacity ahead of the schedule, irrespective of approved calendar plan. Provided further that a block/mine may modify the annual coal production downwards with prior recommendation of competent authority, by providing proper justification. Provided also that the Mining Plan shall include the action plan for the unexplored part of the block, if any, and liquidation of remaining resources to be projectized. (d) The project area envisaged in the Mining Plan must be restricted to the allotted or vested geological block boundary or existing mining lease. A certificate to this effect shall be provided by the Qualified Person (QP) or accredited Mining Plan Preparing Agency (MPPA) that has prepared the Mining Plan. Provided that with permission of the concerned land owner (Central Government or State Government or an individual or any other entity), the project proponent may carry out its activities beyond the allotted or vested geological block boundary or existing mining lease. (e) If any part of an allocated/vested block area cannot be included in the Mining Plan due to constraints such as presence of dense forest (in terms of the Forest Survey of India), dense habitation, rivers, railway lines and other areas that require special permission, such area may be excluded from the Mining Plan. Provided that in case such constraints are removed subsequently, a revised Mining Plan may be submitted for approval. 2.2.2. Safety The project proponent shall ensure that due consideration is paid to safety aspects while preparing and submitting the Mining Plan. 2.2.3. Mechanization: (a) All mines having peak rated capacity of 2 MTPA or more, shall ensure evacuation of coal/lignite through means of transport other than road, within 5 years of commencement of coal production, in case distance between mine and railway siding/ end user is less than 25 km. Provided that in case transportation by road is not avoidable or the distance is more than 25 km and the same is certified by the concerned District Collector(s), the project proponent may construct dedicated road with minimum involvement of public road. (b) All mines shall ensure that the loading infrastructure is mechanized within 5 years of commencement of coal production. The project proponent may choose mining method involving drilling and blasting in coal extraction (excluding overburden removal) only when blast-free technology is not technically feasible or is commercially unviable and shall provide justification for the same. 2.3. Annexures: Along with the Mining Plan, the project proponent shall submit the following documents (as annexures) at the time of submission of the application on the portal: (a) Copy of allotment letter or ownership record. (b) Copy of approval of Board of the company towards submission of Mining Plan.

(c) Copy of certificate as regards preparation of Mining Plan by QP/MPPA along with certificate issued for accreditation by QCI-NABET. (d) Copy of approval of Geological Report. (e) Certificate of QP/MPPA to the effect that the Mining Plan has been prepared within the allotted or vested geological block boundary or existing mining lease area. (f) Copy of analysis as regards deciding on appropriate mining method. (g) Preliminary assessment report in case height of mine openings exceeds 3 metres and/or width exceeds 4.8 metres. (h) Justification for not choosing blast-free technology. 2.4. The format for formulation of the Mining Plan of Coal/ Lignite is at Appendix—II.

Chapter-III Mine Closure Plans 3.1. Mine Closure Plan aims to ensure scientific mine closure and rehabilitation of mining sites, minimising environmental degradation, safeguarding public health, and promoting sustainable development by restoring the land to a condition suitable for future use or returning it to its near-original state or better, while also holding project proponents accountable for their closure obligations. 3.2. Mine closure includes activities such as replanting native or suitable vegetation, restoring water bodies, rehabilitating wildlife habitats and activities related to agriculture, pisciculture, eco- park, recreational, landscaping, waterbody conservation or creation as per Mission Amrit Sarovar, irrigation, solar, green energy and green industries including micro, small and medium enterprises. 3.3. Backfilling of mine void may form part of mine closure activity only where it is carried out specifically for the purpose of mine closure and not as part of regular mining operation. 3.4. Activities undertaken towards just transformation may be audited by third-party agencies appointed by the Central Government (list available at clause 3.14 (vi)). 3.5. Mine Closure Plan shall comprise of (a) Progressive Mine Closure Plan, updated every five years, and (b) Final Mine Closure Plan. Provided that five years before cessation of mining operations, the project proponent shall submit a revised final mine closure plan that shall include operational history of the mine, scientific findings, maps/drawings, monitoring data and expenditure from the escrow account. Provided further that while submitting the revised Final Mine Closure Plan, the project proponent shall submit details of the updated cost estimate for various mine closure activities and balance amount in the escrow account. 3.6. The Action plan for carrying out all mine closure operations (progressive mine closure as well as final mine closure) should be furnished in the format specified in Appendix-III. 3.7. The Final Mine Closure Plan starts towards end of mine life and covers restoring land to its near-original state, repurposing and community development. It includes closure of mine,

dismantling and demolition of structures, removal of machinery, plantation, landscaping, specified post-environmental monitoring, protective and restoration measures, barbed wire fencing, and related activities. 3.8. Final Mine Closure Plan shall contain a completion report containing operational history, past investigation/study/scientific findings and further action taken, if any; mine working maps, images and drawings; mine water discharge and their uses, GPS coordinates for all salient features, safely accessible open portions of mine workings, dumps, area depillared, partially extracted and standing on pillars. 3.9. The Final Mine Closure shall end with post closure monitoring period. 3.10. Surrender of mine after partial extraction: (a) In case of surrender of mine after partial extraction, the CMPDIL shall, within a period of 45 days from receiving intent of such surrender, prepare a temporary mine closure plan for which the cost shall be borne by Project Proponent. (b) The purpose of such temporary mine closure plan is limited to securing the exposed and mined area from safety point of view taking into account the already approved progressive mine closure plan. (c) The project proponent shall carry out activities mentioned in the Temporary Mine Closure Plan prepared by CMPDIL. For this purpose, the project proponent shall not be allowed to utilize the amount available in the escrow account. (d) The project proponent shall be the custodian of the mine until it is reopened or for a period of five (5) years, whichever is earlier. (e) If the mine is not allotted within five (5) years, final mine closure activities shall be undertaken by CMPDIL utilizing the amount available in the escrow account. 3.11. Components of Mine Closure Plan: 3.11.1. A zone of impact should be identified in the project area and buffer zone of 10 km from project boundary to address livelihood and income effects due to mine closure. 3.11.2. Project proponent shall engage local communities and self-help groups through structured consultations and collaborative decision-making to incorporate their perspectives and develop sustainable solutions. 3.11.3. After the closure of mining operations, all social amenities and infrastructure created like hospitals, schools, community centers, office and other buildings should be handed over to the Government or local authorities in consultation with district collector. 3.12. Mine Closure Cost: The project proponent shall deposit amount in the escrow account towards mine closure cost as per calculation indicated at 3.13. The project proponent shall indicate breakup of cost towards individual activities (Appendix--III) of progressive mine closure as well as final mine closure. 3.13. Escrow Amount: (a) The Project Proponent shall open an escrow account in a scheduled commercial bank followed by a tripartite agreement involving CCO before starting mining operations and shall deposit its contribution towards mine closure for that financial year.

(b) The annual rate for deposition towards the escrow account is ₹ 14,00,000 (Fourteen Lakhs per hectare) for opencast mines and ₹ 2,00,000 (Two Lakhs per hectare) for underground mines. These rates shall be the Base Rate as of May 2024 to be escalated on the latest Wholesale Price Index (WPI). Provided that the annual rate for deposition may be revised by the Ministry of Coal. (c) The amount for the first year to be deposited in the escrow account shall be computed by considering the project area multiplied by the escalated rate and dividing the same by the balance production life of the mine in years. (d) The amount as calculated at clause 3.13 (c) shall be compounded @5% annually. Illustration (For OC mines): Total Project Area (Ha) 535.72 Mine Closure Cost per Ha (May 2024) 1400000 WPI as on May 2024 (assumed) 100 Latest WPI available as on date of signing of escrow agreement (assumed) 110 Total Cost (Cr) (110/100*535.72*1400000)=82.5 Production Life of Mine 30 Amount to be deposited in the first year (Cr) 82.5/30=2.75 Amount to be deposited in the second year (Cr) 2.75*1.05=2.89 Amount to be deposited in the third year (Cr) 2.75*1.05*1.05=3.03

(e) The project proponent shall deposit the annual amount for 2nd year onwards in the escrow account for each financial year by 30th September of that year. Provided that an interest @ 1 percent/month shall be charged for the delay in deposition of the amount for every delayed month. Provided further that if project proponent fails to deposit the amount within 30th September of subsequent year, the Coal Controller shall suspend Mining Plan and communicate the same to Ministry of Coal, DGMS, MoEF&CC and the respective State Government. Provided also that once the dues are paid, the suspension order shall be revoked and mining operations may restart. Provided also that upon lapse of six months after the suspension order, if project proponent fails to clear the dues, the Central Government may, on recommendation of the Coal Controller, withdraw approval of the Mining Plan. 3.14. Reimbursement from Escrow Account: (i) Claim for reimbursement from the escrow account may be made by the project proponent up to 50% of the total deposited amount in the previous year (excluding interest accrued) based on work done towards progressive mine closure. (ii) Such claim shall be based on self-certification by authorized official of the company and shall be submitted on or before 31st March of subsequent financial year. (iii) While submitting the claim, videos and georeferenced images of the work done shall be submitted to the office of the Coal Controller for records.

(iv) The coal controller shall, within one month of receipt of claim from the project proponent, allow withdrawal of amount. (v) Every sixth year, eleventh year, sixteenth year and so on, reimbursement from the escrow account may be made to the project proponent up to 50% of the total accumulated amount (excluding interest accrued) based on work done towards progressive mine closure. Provided further that in such years, no annual reimbursement in terms of sub clause 3.14. (i) will be applicable. (vi) Before submission of claim for withdrawal from the escrow account in terms of sub clause (v) above, the project proponent shall get the same verified through one of the following agencies: a. Central Mine Planning and Design Institute (CMPDIL) b. Indian Institute of Technology(ies) or National Institute of Technology (ies) or Engineering colleges controlled by central/state government offering graduate/post-graduate degrees in mining or environmental science c. National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI) d. Any other agency authorized by the Central Government from time to time. (vii) These agencies shall also scrutinize the claim of the project proponent by comparing with Mining Plan. (viii) After submission of claim by project proponent, the steps enumerated at sub clauses 3.14 (ii, iv) above shall be followed. (ix) An illustration as regards the deposition of funds in the escrow account and withdrawal thereof is attached in Appendix-IV. (x) Submission of claims, uploading of report on verification and scrutiny by authorized agencies ( 3.14(vi))  and intimation about scrutinized amount to the project proponent by coal controller shall be done through the dedicated portal. (xi) A minimum of 25% of the balance amount in the escrow account every five-yearly period shall be utilised for community development and livelihood-related activities. An indicative list of activities has been is given in Appendix-V. For Mining Plans already approved, the coal controller shall issue modification to the existing Mining Plans in terms of clause (d) of para 5.1. (xii) 90 percent of the balance amount in the escrow account at the end of the post-closure monitoring period shall be released to the project proponent on completion of all activities of mine closure. 10 percent of the balance deposited amount from final mine closure cost is to be spent towards Just Transformation,  in consultation with district administration, local authority and stakeholders for skill development, sustained livelihood and employment generation etc. (xiii) If the Coal Controller has reasonable grounds for believing that the measures envisaged in the approved mine closure plan will not be carried out, the Coal Controller shall give the Project Proponent a written notice of intention to forfeit the amount in the escrow account. Provided that the decision on such forfeiture shall be made only with the approval of the Central Government.

(xiv) The Project Proponent may re-appropriate funds amongst approved mine closure activities with prior intimation to the Coal Controller. 3.15. Mine Closure Certificate: CCO shall issue the mine closure certificate after the post-closure monitoring period based upon the undertaking by the project proponent and third-party audit report (appointed by the project proponent from a list of agencies as indicated at clause 3.14 (vi)) within a period of 30 days of receipt of such report. Provided that the third-party auditor shall verify that the mine has been closed in all respects as per the Final Mine Closure Plan. Chapter-IV Formulation, submission, scrutiny, approval, revision, and timelines 4.1. Project Proponent shall ensure that the Mining Plan has been prepared by the Qualified Person/ Accredited Mining Plan Preparing Agency recognised under section 22B of the Mineral Concessions Rules, 1960, as amended from time to time. 4.2. Every Mining Plan submitted for approval or revision shall be accompanied by a non- refundable application fee of ₹ 1,00,000 (One Lakh Rupees), which may be revised by the Central Government from time to time. 4.3. Vide notification no. CG-DL-E-01062020-219668 dated 29th May 2020 of the Ministry of Coal, the Coal Controller has been authorised to approve the Mining Plan under sub-section (1) of section 26 read with clause (b) of sub-section (2) of section 5 of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 (67 of 1957). 4.4. For carrying out its functions as required under clause 4.3, the Coal Controller shall be assisted by a Technical Committee that shall scrutinise and examine the Mining Plan submitted by the project proponent. After the scrutiny and examination, the committee shall recommend the Mining Plan to the Coal Controller for "Approval" or "Rejection". 4.5. The Technical Committee shall consist of: a) Deputy Coal Controller - Member Secretary (In case of vacancy, the Coal Controller may designate a suitable officer) b) Director (Technical), MPS, Ministry of Coal- Member c) One officer nominated by Coal Controller. No officer shall serve as member of the committee for more than a year- Member d) An officer not below the rank of General Manager from CMPDIL (nominated by CMD, CMPDIL) in case Mining Plan is not prepared by CMPDIL. No officer shall serve as member of the committee for more than a year- Member 4.6. The members of the Technical Committee shall scrutinise the Mining Plan and submit comments thereof within fifteen (15) days of submission of the Mining Plan on the portal. Non- submission of comments by a member within such period shall imply that the member has no comments to offer.

4.7. On receipt of the comments, the project proponent may consider incorporating the same in the Mining Plan and shall resubmit the modified Mining Plan, within a period of 30 days of expiry of the period mentioned in clause 4.6. Provided that in case the modified Mining Plan, considering the suggestions of members of the Technical Committee, is not resubmitted within such period, the Technical Committee may recommend rejection of the application. Provided further that an opportunity of being heard shall be given to Project Proponent before rejecting application for approval of Mining Plan. 4.8. After the modified Mining Plan has been submitted, a meeting of the Technical Committee shall be convened within 15 days of submission under clause 4.7, wherein the project proponent shall make a presentation before the Technical Committee. 4.9. Technical Committee shall circulate the approved minutes within 7 days of the meeting under clause 4.8. 4.10. The Project Proponent shall incorporate decisions communicated as per minutes of the meeting of Technical Committee and resubmit the Mining Plan within 15 days of issue of minutes of the meeting. 4.11. After final submission of the Mining Plan, a virtual/physical meeting of the Technical Committee may be convened to recommend the approval or rejection of the Mining Plan, taking into consideration the recommendations contained in minutes of the meeting. 4.12. In case of recommendation for rejection, the Technical Committee shall accord the project proponent an opportunity of being heard before its recommendation. The Technical Committee shall record reasons for the rejection. 4.13. After the Technical Committee recommends approval/rejection of the Mining Plan, the Coal Controller shall communicate its decision within 5 days of such recommendation. 4.14. Circulation of Approved Mining Plan: CCO shall circulate a soft copy of the approved Mining Plan along with the approval letter to the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, DGMS, CGWB, State Directorate of Geology and Mining department and District Administration. 4.15. Any person aggrieved by any orders made or directions issued in respect of the Mining Plan by the Coal Controller may apply to the Secretary, Ministry of Coal, for revision of such order made or directions issued thereon. Provided that such application shall be made within a period of 30 (thirty) days of such order made or such direction issued.

Chapter-V Miscellaneous

5.1. Modification or Revision of the Mining Plan: (a) Modifications (minor changes) can be done with the approval of the Board of the respective company.

Provided that any such modifications shall be communicated to the Coal Controller within 30 days of such approval. (b) Revisions (other than minor changes), based on the application in this regard by the project proponent, shall be done only after approval of the Coal Controller. Provided that no revisions shall be approved by the Coal Controller without prior approval of the Nominated Authority if such revisions result in changes in the terms & conditions or efficiency parameters mentioned in CMDPA/CBDPA/LBDPA. (c) An application for Revision of the Mining Plan shall be accompanied by an undertaking to the effect that there have been no violations during the course of mining operations as regards safety, environment and lease-related matters. Provided that in case of violations related to safety (as reported by DGMS), leased area (as reported by State Government authorities), Environment (as reported by Central/State environment authorities), the Project Proponent shall ensure that mitigative measures for such violations are proposed by the project proponent in the application. Provided further that the Coal Controller or the Technical Committee may require the Project Proponent to make a presentation explaining the Revisions. (d) Notwithstanding anything contained in clause 5.1. (a), (b) & (c), the Coal Controller may modify or revise Mining Plan based on directions issued by the central government. 5.2. A report shall be submitted by the project proponent with respect to compliance with the Mining Plan, including deviations, if any, annually to the Coal Controller. 5.3. Through a joint application of project proponents of adjoining mines, a proposal may be submitted for extraction of barrier coal. 5.4. Through mutual agreement, one mine may utilize void/ land of some other mine for purpose of handling overburden, subject to requisite approvals/clearances. 5.5. Mine Repurposing Advisory Committee: A Mine Repurposing Advisory Committee will be set-up in every district where mining operations are carried out in order to oversee implementation of community development and livelihood plan. The Committee shall consist of: a) District Collector, or District officer (as authorised by D.C.) - Chairperson b) Sarpanch/Secretary of Local Gram panchayat – Member c) Representative of reputed NGO (in consultation with D.C.) – Member d) Nodal Officer (Mine Closure) of concerned coal mining company – Member e) Agent of the mine – Member f) Chairperson may nominate two other members, one of which shall be a forest official. Roles of Committee: a) Facilitating periodical meetings and open forums to collaboratively envision and co- create sustainable ideas, consultations, and collaborative decision making.

b) Promoting initiatives that build local knowledge, skills, and resources, such as training programs or alternative livelihood projects, to help the community transition successfully post-mining. c) Ensuring engagement of local communities and self-help groups in Operation & Maintenance of the project and public spaces. d) Ensuring greening of project area through best suited species of plantation and sustainable tourism practices by promoting Geo-Tourism. e) Proactive participation of local community in the domain of selecting skills to be developed to generate alternate economic resources to ensure ‘just-transition’. f) Promote transparency and accountability in community-driven initiatives. 5.6. The district administration may create market mapping of skills, merge income-generating schemes and utilise the District Mineral Fund (DMF). 5.7. Though not mandatory, the project proponent may incorporate the following in the Mining Plan: (a) Make in India: Place a strong emphasis on sourcing indigenous machinery or equipment featuring locally manufactured components. (b) Green Energy and Emission Reduction: Actively strive to meet emission reduction in annual greenhouse gas emissions through renewable sources. (c) Clean Mobility in Mining Operations: Actively promote deployment of electric vehicles (EVs) and gas-based vehicles within coal mine operations. (d) Automation: Look toward the future of mining by exploring and integrating autonomous Heavy Earth Moving Machinery (HEMM) within their sites. (e) Use of blast-free mining technologies (such as longwall/continuous miner) in underground mines. 5.8. Removal of difficulties: Interpretation of the Ministry of Coal as regards provisions of the Guidelines shall be final and binding. 5.9. In the interest of the development of the coal or lignite blocks, the Ministry of Coal may relax or modify any of the provisions of these guidelines. 5.10. In the event of any inconsistency or ambiguity between the provisions of these Guidelines and the Appendices annexed hereto, the provisions of these Guidelines shall prevail and shall be binding to the extent of such inconsistency or ambiguity. 5.11. These Guidelines are without any prejudice to any other relevant rules and regulations issued by concerned government authorities.

Develop & use new scientific methods of agriculture and farming. Support Animal Husbandry. 4. Eco-Tourism Development Convert mined-out areas into eco-tourism hubs with activities like boating, trekking, or cultural tourism in and around project area. 5. Flora and fauna Conservation/Wildlife conservation Reforestation, Eco-parks and Biodiversity Projects [in and around project area]: Reclaim mined land with native species and develop biodiversity parks. Rehabilitate and rejuvenate water bodies affected by mining activities. 7. Clean Energy Projects Implement solar or biogas projects to provide affordable energy to local communities in and around project area. 8. Art and Culture Promote indigenous and local know-hows including promoting traditional practices related to arts, culture and heritage in and around project area. 9. Women Empowerment Initiatives to support women empowerment in and around project area. 10. Welfare of aged and disabled people Special program for welfare of aged and disabled people in and around project area. 11. Sustainable Living In and around project area: Outsourcing of Operation and Maintenance of created assets/ public spaces under mine closure to local communities, self- help groups and project affected person/families. Teach communities about sustainable practices, waste management, and renewable energy. 12. Sanitation In and around project area: Collection, transportation & disposal of waste, cleaning of public places, provision of proper drainage & Sewage Treatment Plant, provision for disposal of fecal sludge, provision of toilet and other related activities. 13. Any other community development project related to mine closure as approved by Mine Closure Advisory Committee.
